studies.title: Working-memory effects of prefrontal tDCS across baseline cognitive-severity groups in schizophrenia: A secondary analysis of a randomized double-blind sham-controlled trial
studies.abstract: Complete-case secondary analysis included 120 of 173 randomized participants (62 active tDCS, 58 sham) who completed the MATRICS Consensus Cognitive Battery (MCCB) before and after 10 bifrontal tDCS sessions. K-means clustering of seven baseline domain T-scores identified cognitive-severity groups. Prefrontal tDCS showed a working-memory signal across both cognitive-severity groups, but baseline severity did not significantly modify treatment response. Results suggest the groups should be interpreted as positions along a cognitive-severity continuum rather than distinct profiles or subtypes. Received June 16, 2026; accepted July 22, 2026.

studies.title: HD-tDCS modulation of the DLPFC-HPC-EC pathway to enhance working memory in schizophrenia: a TMS-EEG Study
studies.authors: Li X, Chen M, Tang E et al.
studies.abstract: High-definition transcranial direct current stimulation (HD-tDCS) targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) modulates the DLPFC-hippocampus-entorhinal cortex (DLPFC-HPC-EC) pathway to enhance working memory in schizophrenia. TMS-EEG was used to assess cortical excitability changes. The study examined the mechanisms by which HD-tDCS applied to the left DLPFC improves working memory performance in patients with schizophrenia, demonstrating that acute cortical excitability change is associated with long-term working memory improvement.

studies.title: Efficacy and safety of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) on treatment-resistant depression (TRD): A systematic review and Meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
studies.abstract: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials evaluating the efficacy and safety of tDCS specifically for treatment-resistant depression (TRD). In six studies with 200 participants, active tDCS led to significantly lower depression scores at the end of treatment compared to sham (standardized mean difference = -1.17). However, a follow-up analysis of delayed effects at 30-day post-treatment found no significant difference between active and sham tDCS. Findings were inconsistent and highly heterogeneous. Significant outcome predictors included session number, age, male percentage, and duration. Standardized, large-scale studies with optimized protocols and longer follow-up are needed to confirm efficacy and safety of tDCS for TRD.

studies.title: Combining repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation with transcranial direct current stimulation in treating psychiatric conditions: A systematic review
studies.abstract: Systematic review of 14 studies combining rTMS with tDCS in treating psychiatric conditions. Conditions covered: unipolar depression (5 studies), bipolar disorder (2), obsessive-compulsive disorder (2), Alzheimer's Disease (1), chronic insomnia (2). For unipolar depression: combined rTMS+tDCS achieved significant reductions in mean Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS) scores (18.22, 16.59 and 20.04 points), with response rates of 83.33% and 91.7% and remission rates of 83.3%, generally superior compared to treatment with rTMS or tDCS alone. For chronic insomnia: greater improvements in sleep quality/efficiency and depressive symptoms compared to monotherapy. Side effects comparable to monotherapy, no significant adverse events reported.

studies.title: Efficacy of high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation on craving in substance use disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis
studies.abstract: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing HD-tDCS vs sham intervention that reported craving as an outcome in substance use disorders. Three RCTs with 138 participants were identified, involving opioid, cannabis, and methamphetamine use disorders. HD-tDCS intervention produced a moderate, statistically significant reduction in craving across substance use disorders with favorable tolerability. The small number of studies and smaller sample size limits generalizability. HD-tDCS may reduce drug craving by stimulating the left and right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC).

studies.title: Prefrontal transcranial direct current stimulation in alcohol use disorder: a pilot randomized sham-controlled trial with exploratory effects on reward craving and depressive symptoms
studies.abstract: Pilot randomized sham-controlled trial of prefrontal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) in patients with alcohol use disorder. Protocol: 1 mA for 20 min per session with maintenance stimulation over 12-week period. Primary outcome: craving severity assessed by Brief Substance Craving Scale (BSCS). Active tDCS did not significantly outperform sham on global craving severity preregistered confirmatory outcomes. Exploratory analyses suggested selective reductions in reward-related craving. tDCS was associated with improvements in depressive symptoms over follow-up. Protocol was well tolerated, supporting further larger neuromodulation trials in alcohol use disorder.

studies.title: The Immediate and Sustained Effects of Multi-Session Biparietal Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation on Insight in Schizophrenia
studies.abstract: 34 participants with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder with impaired insight were randomized to receive either active (n=18) or sham (n=16) biparietal tDCS (anodal: P4; cathodal: P3), administered twice daily over 10 days. Insight assessed using VAGUS Insight into Psychosis scale at baseline pre-treatment, post-treatment, and weekly for 4 weeks. Active tDCS significantly improved average VAGUS scores immediately following and up to 4 weeks post-treatment. Linear mixed-effects models compared estimated marginal mean VAGUS scores between conditions, with and without adjusting for IQ, illness severity, and clozapine use. Biparietal tDCS appears to be a promising intervention for improving insight in schizophrenia.

studies.title: Neuroregulatory effects of combined tDCS and rTMS therapy on major depressive disorder: insights into symptom alleviation and inflammatory modulation
studies.abstract: 186 MDD patients screened; 88 participants enrolled in 4 groups using computerized randomization: combination therapy (tDCS combined with rTMS, n=20), tDCS alone (n=20), rTMS alone (n=21), and pharmacological treatment (n=19), with 80 patients completing the 10-day study. Primary outcome: Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17). Secondary: cytokine levels (inflammatory markers). Combined tDCS and rTMS therapy showed superior symptom alleviation and inflammatory modulation compared to monotherapy groups. Insights into neuroregulatory mechanisms underlying combined non-invasive brain stimulation.
